title: Registration of a Granite Ridge Season Pass and Its Media
content:
A season pass belongs to the person it is registered to, and only the tiers that allow it may be re-registered to someone else.

**Naming the new passholder.** A pass is re-registered only to a person the account holder names in full, and the name given is recorded exactly as stated. The account holder's own statement of that name is what is recorded.

**What re-registration does.** Re-registration places the tier's transfer fee on the pass account, cancels the old media and issues fresh media, and it does not change the tier, the price already committed to or the instalment schedule.

**Tiers that do not allow it.** A tier that does not allow re-registration is not re-registered for any reason, and lending a pass to another person is grounds for the media being confiscated at the lift.

**Replacement media.** Lost, stolen or broken media is replaced at the tier's replacement fee, which is placed on the pass account in the same way.

**When a fee may be placed at all.** A fee is placed on a pass account only while the pass record has not yet reached the expired or closed state. After that point a charge belongs to the following season's record or to the finance team.

**Media at fault.** Where media fails through a fault of the media itself rather than the holder, the replacement is issued at no charge, and that judgement is made at the ticket office when the media is handed in.

### Points of judgement at the counter

*A Granite Ridge Midweek Pass whose holder has moved away.* That tier does not allow re-registration, so the pass is not re-registered whatever the reason given, and no transfer fee arises.

*A Granite Ridge Summit Pass re-registered in January.* The transfer fee of 75.00 is placed on the pass account, fresh media is issued, and the tier, the committed price and the instalment schedule stand exactly as before.

*Media handed in cracked at the lift on a record standing expired.* No fee is placed on that pass account at all, because the record has reached the expired state.

*Media that failed of itself.* The replacement is issued at no charge; the ticket office makes that judgement when the media is handed in.
